gaps.text: Session stickiness: pin a session to the candidate that first served it
gaps.details: Evidence: README.md Roadmap lists session stickiness as not implemented and BLOCKED UPSTREAM (commit 5a2cdd0). Re-verified 2026-09-23 against installed DSH 0.1.5-rc.2: the adapter seam prepareCall(provider, model, signal?) (dsh-llm types index.d.ts:176) still carries no session id; sessionId exists only as GenerateOptions.sessionId (types.d.ts:437), which surfaces at stream time, after the pick. The plugin's pick happens in lib/shim.js:163-191 inside prepareCall with no session context; lib/routing.js keys state per-route only. Done = DSH passes a session id through the prepareCall seam and the router pins a session to its first-serving candidate.

gaps.text: The model-provenance chain defined in the glossary is never recorded or surfaced to the user
gaps.details: GLOSSARY.md glossary defines model provenance as the durable ordered attempt chain for a turn; it is never recorded durably today. Re-verified 2026-09-23: zero llm/attempt markers in ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib (pristine reinstall 2026-08-26 wiped them; durable llm/attempt events exist in old session logs only, all timestamped pre-2026-08-26). What remains is in-process only: lib/shim.js:185-188 builds {route, resolved} inside prepareCall and lib/index.js:148-151 reads payload.provenance in the failover listener; the lib/shim.js:237-240 comment still describes the durable llm/attempt event the runtime no longer emits. README.md:19-21 says the plugin records which real model served each call, visible in the provenance — overstated for the shipped plugin (in-process, lost on restart). Done = a completed turn's attempt chain is durable plugin-side or upstream, never via local runtime patches, and README no longer overstates.

gaps.text: Config schema enumerates only priority|round-robin while the routing engine accepts any registered algorithm
gaps.details: Evidence: commit fc3c302 introduced the pluggable algorithm registry and flagged the config-surface limitation in its commit body; README.md:101 shows the config comment 'priority | round-robin'; examples/least-dispatched.js is a complete custom algorithm the config schema cannot select, while lib/shim.js resolves any registered algorithm id. Done = a route can name any registered algorithm id in config without schema rejection, and an unknown id is rejected with an error listing the registered ids.

gaps.text: KV-cache drift limitation and cache-sensitive routing guidance are gone from the docs
gaps.details: Evidence: commit 1e270dc added an accepted-limitation note and cache-sensitive priority guidance to README; the portfolio rewrite (8776db0, 1897aeb) dropped it — grep for KV or cache across README.md and docs/ today returns 0 hits. The limitation is real and current: round-robin advances a per-route cursor at dispatch (lib/routing.js), so consecutive turns of one conversation can land on different real models and break provider KV-cache prefixes. Done = README or docs/ again carries the accepted-limitation note (round-robin can break provider KV-cache reuse; priority is the cache-safe default) and the gate still passes.

about: DSH plugin that routes virtual model ids to real provider/model candidates with pluggable algorithms and transparent failover
